Reviewed blobs: feature d9cac9f18d129866b9f86c4bb804ab3009ed181d, support 0e73e9929f445764e203daca9dff27b66b94761e - the exact new blobs named in the correction diff's index lines. Scope of this round, per the root dispatch: the recorded finding's correction and the no-secret obligation only; unaffected prior judgments retained.

The correction has three parts and each one is present and load-bearing. (1) Population: planted() (crates/foundry-acceptance/src/support/instance_integration_setup.rs:1823-1840) now lists ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET beside OPERATOR_KEY, OTHER_OPERATOR_KEY, LEGACY_KEY, CLIENT_SECRET, SIGNING_SECRET, OTHER_CLIENT_SECRET and OTHER_SIGNING_SECRET, so every sweep that reads planted() - then_page_shows_nothing_secret (:1879, page body plus redirect location), then_sweep_clean (:1988, every swept page including the Activity list, the process output and the plaintext database) and then_dump_opens_nothing (:1925) - now searches it in all six encodings. Structural fact through the code-fact port: argv 'code-fact query.reads-of ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET --root crates/foundry-acceptance' exit 0, provider textsearch, confidence noisy (degraded: lexical, so same-named symbols and dynamic reads are not distinguished - AST did not answer), index live-source, coverage missing/stale/empty_unindexed all empty, sites = instance_integration_setup.rs:94 (declaration), :320 (Signer::secret), :931 (given_rotated_signing_secret) and the new :1836 (planted). Read directly, :1836 is inside planted()'s value array. (2) Direct reading on the successful rotation: feature line 731 adds 'And the Slack app form offers the client ID "6123456789012.7234567890123" with both secret fields empty' after the save, bound at steps:252-256 to then_form_kept (support:1242), which fails if the form is absent and asserts value(client_id) == the id, value(client_secret) == "" and value(signing_secret) == "". A page that echoed the just-submitted signing secret into the pre-filled form now fails twice - here and in the sweep. (3) Storage and log face: feature line 507 adds 'And Priya has rotated the Slack app's signing secret' to the KPI-IIS-G1 scenario, before the connect Given, and that scenario now carries @us-iis-05. Its Then runs planted(world, true) over the whole database dump, the process output and every swept page, so the rotated value is searched where the page-only sweep cannot look.

Measured RED at this commit, reused not restamped. The acceptance designer's run in the shared local-dev Lima VM, full output /Users/jeffbailey/.cache/nwdes/iis-slack-replace-remove/s1-red-2.txt: argv 'scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c source scripts/eip-lanes.sh; eip_warm; eip_lane us-iis-05', exit 101; stdout ends '1 feature / 10 scenarios (10 failed) / 88 steps (78 passed, 10 failed)' and 'acceptance run failed: 10 step(s) failed, 0 parsing error(s), 0 hook error(s)'. Input-equivalence comparison justifying reuse at this new commit rather than a new execution: the run's 'Defined:' locators are tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature:507:5 (the new KPI rotation Given), :770:5 and :785:5, and 'Matched:' crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs:84:1 and :174:1; sed -n '507p;770p;785p' on the current working-tree file returns exactly those three steps and sed on the steps file returns the rotated-secret given at 84 and the save-app when at 174, while git status is clean and the two changed blobs match the correction diff's new index hashes - so the run consumed byte-identical oracle, support and production inputs in the same VM runtime. I claim no new execution. The run is also this round's constructibility evidence: the acceptance crate compiled ('Compiling foundry-acceptance v0.18.2 ... Finished release profile in 6m 54s'), the lane selected all ten scenarios (nine plus the second outline example) and reported 0 parsing and 0 hook errors, and the designer's gate output /Users/jeffbailey/.cache/nwdes/iis-slack-replace-remove/s1-oracle-smoke-2.txt ends 'xtask smoke :: all gates green'. Every failure is semantic: the KPI-IIS-G1 scenario (output line 52) passes its standalone-process, secrets-key and first-save Givens and then fails on the new rotation Given with the business panic 'Priya finds the Slack app form on the instance integrations page ... Render the form in the page's Slack section ... over a saved app in effect too, with that app's client ID pre-filled and both secret fields empty', the captured body showing /admin/instance/integrations answering 200 OK with the saved-app section and no form. No import error, missing fixture, cross-root path mismatch or fixture-caused provider mismatch appears anywhere in the run.

The no-secret obligation now closes, and the swept population is complete against its denominator. The population is 'every secret value this slice hands Foundry': CLIENT_SECRET 3f9c..., SIGNING_SECRET b7e1..., OTHER_CLIENT_SECRET 0a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9 and OTHER_SIGNING_SECRET 9f8e7d6c5b4a39281706f5e4d3c2b1a0 (the two the refusal outline and the takeover scenario submit) and ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET 0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0 (support:83-94). All five are in planted(); 4 of 4 submitted-and-stored values plus the rotated one, with nothing left out. STRANGER_SIGNING_SECRET is deliberately outside the population: it is never submitted or stored, only used to sign a message Foundry must refuse. The three faces of the promise are each read by a falsifiable observation: the page and its redirect location on the rotation itself (then_page_shows_nothing_secret plus then_form_kept, feature:730-731), and the whole-surface face - every page Priya and Tomas walk, the activity lines inside those bodies, the process output and the plaintext database - on the KPI-IIS-G1 scenario that now rotates first. A Foundry that re-rendered the submitted signing secret, logged it or stored it in the clear fails at least one of them, so the oracle no longer records an observation it does not make.

Side effects of the correction, checked and judged sound. (a) The KPI-IIS-G1 scenario was GREEN before this fix and is now RED until the replace form ships. That is the intended consequence of extending its Given with a behaviour this slice promises, not a regression and not a baseline failure: its failure is the same semantic missing-form panic, and it returns to GREEN with the same implementation every other S1 scenario needs. It is now a completion obligation of this slice, and a reader of the default lane should expect it red before craft. (b) Adding ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET to planted() cannot cause a false failure elsewhere: the sweeps assert absence, so in scenarios that never rotate the extra value is vacuously satisfied, and no page is ever permitted to show it. (c) The rotation Given placed before the connect Given in the KPI scenario strengthens rather than weakens that scenario - connect exchanges Slack's code with the client secret the blank field kept, which the Slack double accepts only when it is exactly the saved one, so a rotation that cleared the client secret now breaks that precondition loudly. (d) acceptance.md's S1 section was updated consistently: its first row's expected text now reads the form handed back with both secret fields empty and 'shows neither key nor secret - the secret she has just submitted included', and a new P1 Covers row is Tested at the KPI-IIS-G1 scenario locator, matching the row list in the bundle. No scope was added beyond the recorded finding's remediation.

Reviewer limits and retained judgments. typesafe: unavailable - capability checked deterministically before any question this round: argv 'env | grep -c ^TYPESAFE_API_KEY=' stdout '0' exit 1, so the authorized client's technical prerequisite is absent exactly as in the previous round (jev_decide.py exit 3 there). No call was fabricated and no blind retry made; the one supported question this round (does the corrected oracle distinguish a Foundry that hands the just-submitted signing secret back from one that keeps it) was answered locally from the oracle bytes and is recorded above. Code facts were resolved through the code-fact port; its answer came from textsearch at noisy confidence, announced as degraded, and was confirmed by reading the named lines. No per-test timing recorded: default budgets apply, no half-budget or derogation statement is in play. Retained from the previous round and not re-litigated: P1 and P2 closure (pre-filled form, blank field keeping the saved client secret falsifiable through the Slack double, no confirm step, the 60-second per-replica observation asked at each replica's own address, the replaced secret refused and the rotated one accepted in separate scenarios, I-11 with the saved universe preserved on four viewers); P6's 'replaced' line read as the whole Activity list; P6's 'removed' arm (expectation E23) out of S1's scope and still a feature completion obligation; the replaced secret observed refused on the single-process Foundry only, judged covered by composition.

diagnostic: Accepted. The one finding that blocked the previous round is corrected at its three faces and no new defect replaces it: planted() now carries ROTATED_SIGNING_SECRET, so every page, page-source, activity, log and plaintext-storage sweep searches the only secret this slice newly introduces; the successful rotation now reads the replace form back directly (then_form_kept: form present, client ID pre-filled, both secret fields empty), so a page that echoed the submitted secret fails twice; and the KPI-IIS-G1 scenario rotates before it connects, putting the rotated value in the whole-database dump and the process output. The swept population is complete against its denominator - all four secrets this slice submits plus the rotated one, with STRANGER_SIGNING_SECRET correctly outside it because it is never stored. RED is measured at these exact bytes and is semantic throughout: exit 101, 10 scenarios, 10 failed, 88 steps (78 passed), 0 parsing and 0 hook errors, every panic naming the missing replace form through a driving-port step, with the new KPI Given failing the same way after its standalone-process, secrets-key and first-save Givens pass; reuse of that run is justified by byte equivalence (clean tree at fcf3022, the two changed blobs matching the correction diff, the run's Defined/Matched locators matching the current lines), not by restamping. No finding remains. Non-blocking and retained: P6's 'removed' arm (E23) is out of S1 and stays a feature completion obligation; the replaced secret is observed refused on the single-process Foundry only, judged covered by composition; KPI-IIS-G1 is now RED until the replace form ships, which is this slice's completion obligation, not a baseline failure; typesafe: unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from the process environment), the one supported question answered locally from the bytes; code facts via code-fact at noisy textsearch confidence, confirmed by reading the lines. Craft may proceed.
